benefits_en:
1. The example of the one who remembers their Lord and the one who does not is like that of the living and the dead.
2. Dhikr is the foundational lifeblood of the human heart and spiritual vitality.

1. Saying 'SubhanAllah wa bihamdihi' 100 times daily erases sins even if they were like the foam of the ocean.
2. The tremendous value of light, consistent glorification on the tongue.

1. Two phrases are beloved to the Most Merciful, light on the tongue, and heavy on the Scale: 'SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi, SubhanAllahil-Azim.'
2. Preserving these two phrases as a daily personal litany.

1. The most beloved words to Allah are four: SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illallah, and Allahu Akbar.
2. The enduring righteous deeds (Al-Baqiyat al-Salihat) that yield eternal fruit.

1. Saying 'La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lahu...' 100 times daily equals freeing ten slaves, writes 100 good deeds, erases 100 sins, and provides all-day protection from Satan.
2. Supreme daily fortress of monotheistic remembrance.

1. 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' (There is no power nor strength except through Allah) is a treasure from beneath the Throne of Allah.
2. Expresses total submission to Allah's power and absolute reliance upon Him.

1. Keep your tongue continuously moist and fresh with the remembrance of Allah.
2. Transforming routine moments into continuous spiritual connection.

1. The solitary devout (Al-Mufarridun) have outpaced all others: those men and women who remember Allah abundantly.
2. Preeminence in spiritual rank achieved through persistent dhikr.

1. Shall I inform you of the best of your deeds, purest with your King, and highest in your ranks? It is the remembrance of Allah.
2. Remembrance of Allah surpasses the spending of gold and silver in spiritual virtue.

1. The Master Supplication for Forgiveness (Sayyid al-Istighfar): acknowledging Allah's lordship, His blessings, one's sins, and seeking His exclusive pardon.
2. Reciting it with conviction in the morning or evening guarantees Paradise for whoever dies that day.

1. Whoever seeks forgiveness for all believing men and women, Allah writes for them a good deed for every single believer.
2. The limitless multiplying reward of expansive, compassionate du'a.

1. Sending blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ: whoever invokes blessing upon him once, Allah blesses them ten times, removes ten sins, and raises them ten ranks.
2. Fulfilling the rights of the Prophet ﷺ and unlocking divine mercy.

1. The closest of people to me on the Day of Resurrection are those who send the most blessings upon me.
2. Cherishing abundance of Salawat on the Prophet ﷺ, especially on Friday.

1. The true miser is the one in whose presence the Prophet's name is mentioned, yet fails to send blessings upon him ﷺ.
2. Guarding the tongue against heedlessness when the noble Prophet is mentioned.

1. Supplication (Du'a) is the essence and core of worship.
2. Manifesting complete poverty, humility, and hope before Allah the Almighty.

1. Whoever does not ask Allah, Allah becomes displeased with them.
2. Allah loves to be petitioned and invoked by His servants continuously.

1. Supplication of a Muslim for their absent brother is answered, and an angel at their side says: 'Ameen, and for you the same.'
2. Sincere altruistic prayer strengthens brotherly bonds and returns blessings upon the supplicant.

1. Three supplications are answered without doubt: the supplication of the oppressed, the traveler, and the parent for their child.
2. Warning against oppressing anyone, as the prayer of the oppressed has no veil between it and Allah.

1. The servant's supplication is answered as long as they do not supplicate for sin, cutting kinship ties, or become impatient saying 'I prayed but was not answered.'
2. Patience, certainty, and perseverance in du'a.

1. Every supplication is granted in one of three ways: immediate granting, storing as reward for the Hereafter, or averting an equivalent evil.
2. No sincere prayer is ever wasted before Allah.

1. The Greatest Name of Allah (Ismullah al-A'zam): invoking Allah by His Oneness, As-Samad, Al-Hayy, Al-Qayyum guarantees divine response.
2. Commencing supplications with comprehensive praises and divine attributes.

1. The Prophet's most frequent supplication: 'Ya Muqallib al-qulub, thabbit qalbi 'ala dinik' (O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion).
2. Human hearts are between the fingers of the Most Merciful; steadfastness is a continuous divine gift.

1. The Prophet's comprehensive prayer: 'Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah wa fil-akhirati hasanah wa qina 'adhaban-nar' (Our Lord, grant us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the Fire).
2. Encompasses all lawful worldly needs and eternal success.

1. Supplicating for guidance, piety, chastity, and self-sufficiency: 'Allahumma inni as'alukal-huda wat-tuqa wal-'afafa wal-ghina.'
2. The four golden pillars of spiritual and moral excellence.

1. Seeking refuge from the decline of Allah's blessings, the transformation of His well-being, sudden vengeance, and all of His anger.
2. Preserving gratitude and remaining vigilant against sudden trials.

1. Seeking refuge in Allah from anxiety, sorrow, incapacity, laziness, cowardice, miserliness, the burden of debt, and being overpowered by men.
2. Comprehensive psychological, physical, and financial fortress.

1. Seeking refuge from severe calamity, falling into misery, an evil decree, and the malicious gloating of enemies.
2. Protecting one's spiritual, physical, and familial safety.

1. Seeking refuge from evil character traits, corrupt desires, and debilitating illnesses.
2. Maintaining moral refinement and asking for wholesome health.

1. Seeking refuge from the evil of what one has done and the evil of what one has not done.
2. Complete humility and acknowledgement of human vulnerability before divine justice.

1. Seeking refuge in the Perfect Words of Allah from the evil of what He has created: 'A'udhu bi kalimatillahi at-tammati min sharri ma khalaq.'
2. Protection from venomous creatures, malevolent spirits, and physical harm when stopping at any destination.

1. Saying 'Bismillahilladhi la yadurru ma'asmihi shay'un...' three times morning and evening guarantees immunity from all sudden harm.
2. Invoking the protective Name of Allah over heaven and earth.

1. Supplication when leaving the house: 'Bismillahi tawakkaltu 'alallah, la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.'
2. The angels proclaim: 'You are guided, defended, and protected,' and Satan departs in defeat.

1. Supplication when entering the home: mentioning Allah upon entering and upon eating prevents Satan from sleeping or dining in the house.
2. Sanctifying domestic spaces with daily remembrance.

1. Supplication before marital intimacy: 'Bismillah, Allahumma jannibnash-Shaytana wa jannibish-Shaytana ma razaqtana.'
2. Divine protection for any resulting offspring against the harm of Satan.

1. Supplication before entering the restroom: 'Allahumma inni a'udhu bika minal-khubuthi wal-khaba'ith' (O Allah, I seek refuge in You from male and female impure spirits).
2. Preserving modesty and seeking spiritual shielding in places of filth.

1. Supplication when exiting the restroom: 'Ghufranak' (I seek Your forgiveness).
2. Expressing gratitude for the removal of bodily harm and seeking spiritual purification.

1. Supplication when boarding a ride or vehicle: 'Subhanalladhi sakh-khara lana hadha wa ma kunna lahu muqrinin...'
2. Remembering the Creator's subjugation of travel means and reflecting on the journey of life.

1. The traveler's comprehensive travel prayer: asking for piety, righteous deeds, ease of journey, and protection for family and wealth.
2. Entrusting one's dependents and possessions into Allah's safe custody during absence.

1. Supplication when experiencing anxiety or distress: 'La ilaha illallahul-'Azimul-Halim, La ilaha illallahu Rabbul-'Arshil-'Azim...'
2. Overcoming distress through pure contemplative praise of the Lord of the Throne.

1. Supplication of Prophet Yunus (AS) in the belly of the whale: 'La ilaha illa Anta, Subhanaka, inni kuntu minaz-zalimin.'
2. No distressed believer ever invokes Allah with this prayer except that Allah delivers them from grief.

1. Supplication for paying debts: 'Allahummakfini bi halalika 'an haramik, wa aghnini bi fadlika 'amman siwak.'
2. Divine assistance in settling debts and gaining independence from reliance on creation.

1. Supplication when visiting the sick: placing one's hand and praying seven times: 'As'alullahal-'Azim, Rabbal-'Arshil-'Azim an yashfiyak.'
2. Bringing comfort, optimism, and spiritual healing to the afflicted.

1. Supplication when consoling the bereaved: 'Inna lillahi ma akhadha wa lahu ma a'ta, wa kullu shay'in 'indahu bi ajalin musamma, faltasbir wal-tahtasib.'
2. Reaffirming divine ownership, appointed lifespans, and the necessity of patient trust.

1. Supplication when struck by calamity: 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un, Allahumma-jurni fi musibati wa akhlif li khayran minha.'
2. Sincere submission transforms worldly loss into superior divine compensation (as experienced by Umm Salamah).

1. Supplication upon hearing thunder: 'Subhanalladhi yusabbihur-ra'du bi hamdihi wal-mala'ikatu min khifatih.'
2. Awe and reverence of natural forces glorifying their Creator.

1. Supplication when rain falls: 'Allahumma sayyiban nafi'an' (O Allah, make it a beneficial downpour).
2. Welcoming divine nourishment and praying for fertility and safety.

1. Supplication upon sighting the new crescent moon: asking for safety, faith, peace, Islam, and guidance.
2. Synchronizing monthly calendar rhythms with spiritual aspirations.

1. Supplication when breaking the fast: 'Dhahabad-zama'u wabtallatil-'uruqu wa thabatal-ajru in sha' Allah.'
2. Gratitude for physical refreshment alongside certainty of eternal spiritual reward.

1. Supplication when wearing new garments: praising Allah who provided clothing and asking for its good and protection from its evil.
2. Cultivating gratitude for daily provisions and rejecting vanity.

1. Supplication before sleeping: performing Wudu, lying on the right side, reciting Surat al-Ikhlas/Mu'awwidhat, Ayat al-Kursi, and the night prayers.
2. Concluding each day in complete surrender, ready to meet the Lord.

1. Supplication upon waking up: 'Alhamdulillahilladhi ahyana ba'da ma amatana wa ilayhin-nushur.'
2. Morning renewal of gratitude for the gift of life and consciousness of Resurrection.

1. Supplication when rising during the night (Tahajjud): praising Allah as the Light and Sustainer of the heavens and earth.
2. Intimate theological adoration before beginning night vigil prayer.

1. Sincere repentance (Tawbah) erases all preceding sins; whoever repents from sin is like one who has no sin.
2. Keeping the doors of divine mercy wide open for every returning servant.

1. Allah rejoices more over the repentance of His servant than a traveler who loses his mount with all food and water in a barren desert, then wakes up to find it standing right beside him.
2. The boundless love and pleasure Allah takes in the penitent soul.

1. The Prophet ﷺ himself sought forgiveness and turned to Allah in repentance more than seventy or one hundred times every day.
2. Sincere Istighfar is the continuous practice of the most elevated souls.

1. Allah extends His Hand during the night so that the sinner of the day may repent, and extends His Hand during the day so that the sinner of the night may repent, until the sun rises from the west.
2. Perpetual invitation to return to Allah without delay.

1. Allah accepts the repentance of a servant as long as the death rattle (Ghargharah) has not reached the throat.
2. Urging immediate repentance before the final moments of life arrive.

1. The story of the man who killed ninety-nine souls, completed it to one hundred, then sincerely sought repentance and died while migrating toward the land of righteousness; Allah forgave him.
2. No sin is too vast for the forgiveness of Allah when repentance is sincere.

1. Every son of Adam errs continuously, and the best of those who err are those who constantly repent.
2. Human fallibility is met with persistent, proactive repentance.

1. Follow up a bad deed with a good deed; the good deed will wipe it out, and treat people with beautiful character.
2. Active moral redemption and maintaining righteous conduct.

1. If you were not to sin, Allah would replace you with people who sin and ask Allah for forgiveness, and He would forgive them.
2. Manifests the divine attributes of Al-Ghafur (The All-Forgiving) and Al-Rahim (The Especially Merciful).

1. Hadith Qudsi: 'O Son of Adam, so long as you call upon Me and hope in Me, I forgive you for whatever you have done and I do not mind...'
2. The ocean of divine pardon overshadows human shortcomings.

1. Sincere regret in the heart is the cornerstone of repentance (Al-Nadamu tawbah).
2. Feeling deep remorse over transgression inspires genuine transformation.

1. Whoever regularly seeks forgiveness (Istighfar), Allah creates for them a way out from every distress, relief from every anxiety, and provides for them from places they never imagined.
2. Istighfar unlocks spiritual relief and material abundance.

1. The Salat al-Tawbah (Prayer of Repentance): performing Wudu, praying two rak'ahs, and asking Allah for forgiveness guarantees divine pardon.
2. Practical ritual mechanism for immediate spiritual cleansing after committing an error.

1. Honoring parents is the greatest deed after the prayer at its proper time; Paradise lies beneath the feet of mothers.
2. Prioritizing service and gentleness toward parents above all voluntary deeds.

1. A man asked: 'Who among people is most deserving of my good company?' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Your mother' three times, then 'Your father.'
2. Triple emphasis on the mother due to pregnancy, childbirth, and nursing.

1. The pleasure of the Lord is in the pleasure of the parents, and the anger of the Lord is in the anger of the parents.
2. Connecting filial devotion directly with attaining divine favor.

1. Disobedience and disrespect to parents (Uquq al-Walidayn) is among the most catastrophic major sins.
2. Warning that mistreatment of parents brings severe retribution in this world before the next.

1. Upholding ties of kinship (Silat al-Rahim) expands one's sustenance (Rizq) and prolongs one's lifespan and blessed legacy.
2. Family solidarity directly attracts divine blessing and longevity.

1. The true upholder of kinship is not the one who merely reciprocates, but the one who restores ties when relatives sever them.
2. Exemplary moral nobility in overcoming family estrangement.

1. The severed womb clings to the Throne of the Most Merciful saying: 'Whoever maintains me, Allah maintain him; whoever severs me, Allah sever him.'
2. Terrifying danger of abandoning close family and blood relatives.

1. The one who severs ties of kinship will not enter Paradise.
2. Sincere reconciliation with estranged family is an urgent religious obligation.

1. Angel Jibril kept emphasizing the rights of the neighbor until the Prophet ﷺ thought he would grant the neighbor a share of inheritance.
2. High sacred status and inviolable rights of neighbors in Islam.

1. By Allah he does not believe! He whose neighbor is not safe from his harmful conduct and malice.
2. Good treatment and protection of neighbors is a direct criterion of genuine faith.
